source_text.GH#2583: managed_by: core Records callers (RecordDeadlineSweep; future engine step writes and scripts) bypass the route-level managed-type guard. ACs: (1) enumerate and classify every core caller of Records.create/update/delete; (2) move the enforcement point so no core path writes a managed type without an explicit typed ownership proof, with a boundaries/CI check against new unguarded callers; (3) RecordDeadlineSweep proves ownership or is shown to touch no managed type, with a test; (4) coordinate with REQ-484 / 0054 so step writes use the same check. Gates SECURITY-REVIEWER (INV-6), REVIEWER. Issue comments: one heartbeat, no AC revision.

task.description: WF-03 step 1 diagnosis for GH #2583. No fix, no lib/ or test edits, no mix (supervisor constraint): reproduction is by code reading plus an existing passing test that exercises the bypass.

result.summary: DIAGNOSIS (CONFIRMED on main c55baa4f5 by code reading and by an existing test; mix not run per dispatch constraint). Security gap, not a regression. ROOT CAUSE: the managed_by write lock (REQ-496 / GH #2530, 0050 D7) is enforced ONLY in the HTTP router (lib/letflow/routers/entities.ex:2727 guard_tenant_write/3 -> ManagedTypes.check_tenant_write/2, wrapped around create :993, update :1047, delete :1098, import :1179). Letflow.Entities.Records (records.ex:233 create_record/2, :294 update_record/2, :343 delete_record/2) has no ownership parameter and never reads EntityDefinition.managed_by, although it already loads the active definition row (fetch_active_definition, records.ex:968) on every command. So ANY in-process caller writes a managed type. Proof that runs today: test/letflow/routers/entities_managed_by_test.exs:412 'T-06' asserts {:ok, _} for create+update of every managed fxm type through Letflow.Modules.FixtureManaged.create_record/3 (test/support/modules/fixture_managed/fixture_managed.ex:72,87,102), which is a plain Records.create_record/2 call with NO ownership proof; the same call from any other module would succeed identically. Secondary: the router check is a separate read outside the Records transaction (check-then-act); harmless today because a name can only become managed when it has no row at all (ManagedTypes.claim_unmanaged_name, managed_types.ex:171), but a check on the resolved definition row inside Records removes the window. Why tests missed it: 0050 D7 placement note (0050:177-181) deliberately put the lock at the router because modules call Records directly; REQ-496 scoped core callers out (requirements.yaml REQ-496 OUT OF SCOPE: 'managed_by checks on process-step entity writes (REQ-484)'). KEY INVARIANT (verified from managed_types.ex:140-178): for a managed name EVERY entity_definitions row carries the same managed_by (first row stamped at claim; later rows only by the claiming Owner, which stamps; tenant creates refused; an Owner never claims a name with any existing row), and the column is trigger-immutable. Hence definition.managed_by of the row Records already fetched == owner_of(name): Records can enforce with zero extra queries. CALL-SITE TABLE (complete grep of lib/, priv/, test/support, lib/mix/tasks for create_record|update_record|delete_record calls, incl. fully-qualified; there is NO Records import function, import is router-only; no other writer of entity_record_latest or ENTITY_RECORD_* events exists outside records.ex except Record.Projector rebuild, projector.ex:285, which replays existing events and is not a new write): [1] routers/entities.ex:1008 create (POST /entities/records/:type) -- HTTP, guarded at :993 -- can touch managed: NO (refused 403 first) -- classify: TENANT, refuse managed (pass :tenant). [2] entities.ex:1067 update (PUT) -- guarded :1047 -- NO -- TENANT. [3] entities.ex:1116 delete (DELETE) -- guarded :1098 -- NO -- TENANT. [4] entities.ex:1319 create per import entry (POST .../import) -- guarded :1179 -- NO -- TENANT. [5] modules/exam/anti_cheat.ex:258 create 'session_event' -- exam module, candidate request -- NO today (exam manifest lib/letflow/modules/exam/exam.ex:41 declares no manages_entity_types; pack types unmanaged) -- TENANT semantics (unmanaged-type writer); would need its Owner only if exam ever declares managed types. [6] modules/exam/certificate.ex:335 create 'certificate' (idempotency_match :target) -- exam issuance -- NO -- same as [5]. [7] modules/exam/session.ex:1064 update 'session_answer' -- NO -- same. [8] session.ex:1263 update 'session' (submit) -- NO -- same. [9] session.ex:1328 write_record/4 -> create, used for 'session' :759, 'session_question' :907, 'session_answer' :1081, 'session_question_score' :1242 -- NO -- same. [10] scheduler/record_deadline_sweep.ex:254 update, entity_type from deploy config :deadline_sweep rules (system actor nil-UUID) -- CAN touch a managed type if an operator configures a rule on one (config is arbitrary; no rule is configured in config/*.exs today, only tests put_env) -- classify: MUST BE REFUSED (core, not a module, holds no Owner; 0054 D12 'no entity write from timers'). [11] lib/mix/tasks/letflow.seed.exam_fixtures.ex:577 create exam pack types (category, tag, exam, question, answer_option...) -- seed -- NO -- TENANT semantics. [12] test/support/exam_fixtures.ex:220 create_record!/4 -- test fixture, exam types -- NO -- TENANT semantics. [13-15] test/support/modules/fixture_managed/fixture_managed.ex:72/87/102 create/update/delete -- test fixture standing in for an owning module -- YES (that is its purpose) -- MODULE-OWNED, must pass its Owner. Engine step writes: none exist yet (EntityPort/StepWrites/command_multi NOT FOUND on main); per 0054 option A they are TENANT semantics (refuse managed, REQ-499 also refuses at activation); REQ-501 handlers are MODULE-OWNED via Owner. Test callers outside test/support: 217 direct calls in 24 test/*.exs files; none writes a managed type (no file using FixtureManaged calls Records directly). RECOMMENDED ENFORCEMENT DESIGN (mirror create_definition/2,/3, definitions.ex:107,135): add create_record/3, update_record/3, delete_record/3 taking authority :: ManagedTypes.owner() (:tenant | %Owner{}); keep the /2 arities as delegates passing :tenant (fail-closed default, zero churn for the 13 lib and 217 test call sites; only FixtureManaged's 3 calls change). One private check_write_authority(definition, entity_type, authority) run right after fetch_active_definition and BEFORE ensure_mutable (so it precedes the append-only 422, the record lookup and the already-deleted no-op, matching the router's order and leaking nothing): managed_by nil -> :ok for any authority; managed_by M and authority %Owner{module_id: M, manages: S} with entity_type in S -> :ok; otherwise {:error, :entity_type_managed}; any other authority term -> FunctionClauseError. Router keeps guard_tenant_write (constant 403 before the body is read) and adds a render_record_command clause mapping {:error, :entity_type_managed} to Error.entity_type_managed/0 (reachable only via the race). Sweep needs NO code change: it keeps /2 (:tenant), a rule on a managed type gets {:error, :entity_type_managed} per record, rolls back that one record (record_deadline_sweep.ex:200-204), logs, continues -- AC3 'shown to touch no managed type' by construction. AC3 test: install FixtureManaged, create a due org_unit-shaped managed record via the owner path, put_env a rule on it, run RecordDeadlineSweep.run/2 -> :ok, record field_values unchanged, no new ENTITY_RECORD_UPDATED event; control rule on fxm_free transitions. OWNER PROVENANCE / CI CHECK: Owner is buildable only in managed_types.ex and module_owner/1 callable only in installs.ex, pinned by the AST test test/letflow/entities/managed_types_callers_test.exs (T-34; check_boundaries cannot express per-function allow-lists, managed_types.ex:17-20). Extend that AST test: (a) a Records.create_record/update_record/delete_record (and later command_multi) call whose authority argument is anything but the literal :tenant may appear only in allow-listed files (initially none in lib/; test/support is outside the lib scan); (b) widen the module_owner( allow-list only for the runtime Owner sources chosen below. Because /2 is fail-closed, a new unguarded caller can never write a managed type; the AST test guards where a real Owner comes from. Optionally mirror it as a textual mix task in mix.exs @check_static_steps (:165) like letflow.check_scope_node_paths_writers. HOW MODULES GET AN OWNER AT RUNTIME (exam does not need one today): Owner is currently minted only at install time. Options for the designer: (i) allow ManagedTypes.module_owner(EntryModule) in files under lib/letflow/modules/<id>/ only when the argument is that directory's own entry module (AST-checkable via the manifest id); (ii) a generated owner/0 on the entry module (defmanifest) that calls module_owner(__MODULE__), callable only from its own directory. Either way Records' manages-membership check bounds the Owner to the module's own declared types. REQ-501 HANDLERS: StepWrites (the single EntityPort impl) resolves module_id -> entry module via Letflow.Modules.Catalog.fetch/1, verifies the pinned owner_module stamp/hash (0054 D6), then builds the Owner (allow-list StepWrites for module_owner( in T-34) -- preferably narrowed to the handler's registered target types (a new ManagedTypes constructor, e.g. handler_owner/2, manages = handler targets), which also enforces REQ-501's 'handler writes outside its registered target list is refused' -- and passes it in the handler ctx; the handler forwards it to Records.command_multi. COORDINATION WITH REQ-499 (#2587 PR A) / 0054 D2.3: command_multi/3 (new) must take the same authority (StepWrites passes :tenant for declarative lines, so a managed type is refused at runtime by Records too, not only by StepWrites' own check) and must call the SAME check_write_authority on the definition it reads under lock, so the single-command and multi paths share one check. Recommended order: land #2583 first (smaller, adds the private check), then REQ-499 PR A reuses it; if PR A lands first it must add the authority parameter to command_multi in the same shape. 0054 D6's 'until the stamp exists ... managed_by types cannot be written by a step: REFUSE' is satisfied by :tenant authority. OVERLAP: open PRs (gh pr list, 2026-10-14T21:23Z): #2594 (GH #2552 token issuer), #2593 (GH-2534 7b-2b scripts SoD), and stale chore/docs PRs #1121 #1116 #1109 #1107 #765 #342 #340; NONE touches records.ex, routers/entities.ex, managed_types.ex, the sweep, installs.ex, catalog.ex or exam modules (checked per-PR file lists). No remote branch for #2587/#2550/#2590 exists; local sibling worktrees have no diff on those files. #2550 (idempotency namespace, OPEN) and REQ-499 PR A both plan edits to records.ex (sys: refusal, command_multi) -> textual conflict risk, sequence merges. REQ-499/REQ-501 have NO entry in docs/requirements.yaml yet (only GH #2587/#2590). OPEN QUESTIONS FOR CODE-DESIGNER: Q1 keep /2 as :tenant delegates (recommended) or force an explicit /3 everywhere (217 test edits, no security gain)? Q2 runtime Owner source for modules: (i) vs (ii) above, and whether to add it now (no production consumer until the org/WMS modules) or only the FixtureManaged path now. Q3 error shape from Records: reuse {:error, :entity_type_managed} (same atom as router and check_create) -- recommended; add to the command_error type. Q4 should the sweep additionally validate rules up front (skip a managed-type rule with one warning per tick instead of one per due record)? Optional; the per-record refusal already satisfies AC3. Q5 exam types are unmanaged and therefore writable through the generic routes by :EntitiesRecordsWrite holders (session/certificate tampering); REQ-496 explicitly did not retrofit exam -- out of #2583 scope, flag as a possible follow-up issue rather than widening this one. Q6 should T-34's new rule also forbid passing an Owner through variables (only a direct module_owner/handler_owner result), or accept any non-literal in allow-listed files only? SECURITY: INV-6 applies (core write path gains an authority check; no new route, no migration); INV-1 unchanged (prefix still explicit). Gates: SECURITY-REVIEWER and REVIEWER required. MIGRATION: none. Severity MEDIUM: no production module declares manages_entity_types yet, so no live managed type is exposed today, but it is a hard prerequisite of REQ-501 / WMS ledger (#2590) and of the org module.
